description: Selected reported VIPeR rank-one results, not a complete state-of-the-art history or a controlled re-evaluation.
caveat: This is a selected history, not a leaderboard. Historical methods and unseen-target domain generalization are separated. Training sources, pretraining, parameter selection, and randomized evaluation procedures differ even within each group. Approximate values are labeled explicitly.

results.source_location: Figure 6, right-hand CMC plot, PDF page 5
results.protocol: Original 5x2 evaluation with 316-image galleries. Approximately 5 percent read from the highest rank-one baseline in the figure; not a tabulated value. This variant includes manually localized body regions.
An even identity train/test split; randomized assignment of paired images to gallery/probe, averaging both directions. The text states around 12 percent.

results.source_location: Section 4, VIPeR experiment, PDF page 6; Figure 4
results.protocol: Average over 10 random sets of 316 pedestrians. Feature weights selected using the first 100 VIPeR pairs. The text states around 20 percent.
Random 316-identity training and test sets, averaged over 100 runs. The chart uses the average, not the best-run 22 percent result.

results.variant: eSDC ocsvm, combined with wHSV and MSCR
results.protocol: Half the identities used for fitting without identity labels, half for testing; average of both probe/gallery directions over 10 trials. Uses the best eSDC variant, not the 26.31 percent kNN variant.
Disjoint half-identity train/test split, camera A probes and camera B gallery; average over 10 trials. Reported standard deviation 1.23 percentage points.
Half-identity train/test splits, both gallery/probe directions, averaged over 100 trials. The 37.8 percent result includes feature fusion, not standalone SCNCD.
Random half-identity train/test splits, averaged over 10 trials. Standalone LOMO + XQDA, excluding the separate LADF fusion result.
Half-identity train/test split averaged over 10 partitions; ensemble of multiple features and nonlinear base metrics. Original figure reports 45.89 percent; later tables round to 45.9.
316 training and 316 test identities, 10 random trials. Includes gallery-dependent context analysis and re-ranking; not an independent pairwise matcher.

results.variant: GOGFusion + XQDA, with patch weights and color-space fusion
results.protocol: Random half-identity train/test splits, averaged over 10 splits. Reported result includes GOG color-space fusion and XQDA metric learning.
Half-identity train/test splits, averaged over 10 trials. Kernelized null-space learning with score-level fusion of LOMO and a second histogram-based descriptor.

Unseen VIPeR target, 10 random evaluation splits; trained on Market-1501, DukeMTMC-reID, CUHK02, CUHK03, and CUHK-SYSU. The alternative four-source setting including MSMT17 reports 55.1 percent (supplementary Table 2); not silently mixed here.

Protocol 1: unseen VIPeR target, same five source datasets as the SNR point, 10 random evaluation splits. Protocol 2 uses Market-1501, DukeMTMC-reID, CUHK03, and MSMT17 and reports 63.4 percent instead.

Protocol 1: unseen VIPeR target, trained on Market-1501, CUHK02, CUHK03, and CUHK-SYSU; DukeMTMC omitted. Average over 10 random query/gallery splits. Source pool therefore differs from SNR and RaMoE.
Protocol 1: unseen VIPeR target, trained on Market-1501, CUHK02, CUHK03, and CUHK-SYSU; average of 10 random evaluation splits.

results.publication: IEEE TIFS 2025, DOI 10.1109/TIFS.2025.3536608; title spells the acronym CILP-FGDI, while the method/code use CLIP-FGDI
results.source_location: Section IV-A and Table I, PDF pages 5-6; authors' datasets/viper.py for gallery size
results.protocol: Protocol 1: CLIP-pretrained ViT, trained for re-ID on Market-1501, CUHK02, CUHK03, and CUHK-SYSU, with no VIPeR target training. Authors' loader uses 316-image galleries. Main table reports averages of three experiments; the best hyperparameter ablation in Table VIII reports 77.5 percent, not used as the main milestone.
